summary: Yosho Nomura (1916–1997) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1936–1939). He later served as a professor at Rissho University (~1961–1987) and directed the Institute for the Comprehensive Study of the Lotus Sutra (attested 1981–1985).

Youru Wang is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Temple University under Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Thomas J. Dean. Wang held posts at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (1999) and Rowan University (attested 2007–2018).
Youwei Kang (1858–1927) was a Chinese philosopher and sinologist. In 1890, he founded Wanmu Caotang, where he taught Qichao Liang and held a post from circa 1891 to 1898.

Yozo Taniyama (born 1972) is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at Tohoku University (~1991–1996). He held posts at Shitennoji University, St. Thomas University, Sophia University, and Tohoku University's Department of Practical Religious Studies (~2012).
Yu Yan Pang is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of Jing Yin and Cecilia Chan, having also studied under Eric Kvan.

Yu-Chen Tsui is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed master's studies at Columbia University under Chün-fang Yü, pursued doctoral studies supervised by Natasha Heller, and studied under traditional teacher Sheng Yen.

Yu-kwan Ng (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at The Chinese University of Hong Kong and earned a PhD from McMaster University (~1979–1985). He held posts at Hong Kong Baptist University (1988) and National Central University (~2001).

Yu-min Lee is a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied under graduate supervisor John C. Huntington. Lee held a post as professor at National Taiwan University (attested 2002).
Yuan Ren is a scholar in Buddhist studies and sinology who earned a PhD at McMaster University (attested 1998) under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff.

Yuanxing Guo (1920–1982) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Gongga Rinpoche. Guo held posts at the Jinling Scriptural Press and as a researcher at the Research Institute of Chinese Buddhism.

Yuanying (1878–1953) was a Buddhist studies figure who served as abbot of Jiedai, Tiantong, and Yongquan temples. He founded the Sengmin School (1917) and Yuanming Lengyan School (1945), and was president of the Buddhist Association of China (1929, 1953).
Yudru Tsomu is a Tibetologist and historian who completed a PhD at Harvard University under Leonard van der Kuijp, with additional advising from Mark Elliott, Janet Gyatso, and Philip A. Kuhn.

Yuen Ren Chao (1892–1982) was a linguist and sinologist who studied at Cornell (~1910–1914) and Harvard (~1915–1918). He held academic posts at Cornell (~1919–1920), Harvard (~1921–1924), Tsinghua University (~1925–1929), and the University of California, Berkeley (~1947–1963).
Yuexia (1858–1917) was a Buddhist studies figure who founded Huayan University and served there as a teacher.

Yuguang Liu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Northwest Minzu University in 2000 and completed a PhD at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (attested 2005).
Yuhiko Katsuzaki (born 1946) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (~1965–1974). Katsuzaki later served as president of Taisho University from circa 2011 to 2015.
Yui Chi Lau (1914–1997) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Ying-Kuang Chu. Lau founded the Hong Kong Vajrayana Esoteric Society and taught Shek-Wing Tam.

Yui Suzuki is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and art history/archaeology who completed doctoral studies at UCLA under William M. Bodiford, Lothar von Falkenhausen, and Donald F. McCallum. Suzuki held a post at the University of Maryland, College Park (attested 2012).

Yuichi Kajiyama (1925–2004) was a Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology scholar educated at Kyoto University, Nava Nalanda Mahavihara, SOAS, and Vienna. He held long-term posts at Kyoto University (1956–1988), Bukkyo University (1988–1997), and Soka University (1997–2001).

Yuichi Shionoya (1932–2015) was a scholar of philosophy and other fields who studied at Nagoya University (~1951–1953) and Hitotsubashi University (~1953–1961). Shionoya later held an academic post at Nagoya University from circa 1964 to 1974.
